PROC PRINT

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-proc-print.Rmd
guide-proc-print.Rmd
library(sasonr)

PROC PRINT lists the observations of a data set. sasonr writes the listing as text laid out at LINESIZE, and the table in the HTML or RTF document when one of those destinations is open. The examples use one small invented data set.

prog <- "
options nocenter;
data vitals;
  input subj $ arm $ visit sbp dbp;
  label sbp = 'Systolic BP' dbp = 'Diastolic BP';
  datalines;
S01 A 1 128 82
S01 A 2 124 80
S02 A 1 135 88
S02 A 2 131 85
S03 B 1 118 76
S03 B 2 121 79
;
run;
"

A plain listing

The Obs column numbers the observations; numbers without a format are right-aligned and the column headings are centred over their columns.

res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#> Obs    subj    arm    visit    sbp    dbp
#> 
#>  1     S01      A       1      128     82
#>  2     S01      A       2      124     80
#>  3     S02      A       1      135     88
#>  4     S02      A       2      131     85
#>  5     S03      B       1      118     76
#>  6     S03      B       2      121     79

VAR, ID and NOOBS

VAR chooses and orders the columns; ID replaces the Obs column by a variable; NOOBS drops it.

res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals; id subj; var visit sbp dbp; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#> subj    visit    sbp    dbp
#> 
#> S01       1      128     82
#> S01       2      124     80
#> S02       1      135     88
#> S02       2      131     85
#> S03       1      118     76
#> S03       2      121     79

Labels and SPLIT=

LABEL uses the variable labels as headings. A label wider than its column is split at blanks; SPLIT= names the character where the heading breaks.

res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "proc print data=vitals noobs label; var subj sbp dbp; run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#>         Systolic    Diastolic
#> subj       BP           BP
#> 
#> S01        128          82
#> S01        124          80
#> S02        135          88
#> S02        131          85
#> S03        118          76
#> S03        121          79

BY groups, SUM and N

With BY the data must be sorted by the BY variables; each group gets its BY line. SUM adds the group totals and the grand total.

res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=vitals; by arm; run;
proc print data=vitals noobs;
  by arm;
  var subj visit sbp;
  sum sbp;
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#> arm=A
#> 
#> subj    visit    sbp
#> 
#> S01       1      128
#> S01       2      124
#> S02       1      135
#> S02       2      131
#> ----             ---
#> arm              518
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> arm=B
#> 
#> subj    visit    sbp
#> 
#> S03       1      118
#> S03       2      121
#> ----             ---
#> arm              239
#>                  ===
#>                  757

N writes the number of observations of each group.

res <- sas_run(paste(prog, "
proc sort data=vitals; by arm; run;
proc print data=vitals noobs n;
  by arm;
  var subj sbp;
run;"))
cat(res$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#> arm=A
#> 
#> subj    sbp
#> 
#> S01     128
#> S01     124
#> S02     135
#> S02     131
#> 
#> N = 4
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> arm=B
#> 
#> subj    sbp
#> 
#> S03     118
#> S03     121
#> 
#> N = 2

Tables wider than the line

The gap between columns is 4 blanks, or 3, 2, 1 when that makes the table fit on the line. When it does not fit with a gap of 1, variable names wider than one-position values are written down the columns; otherwise the columns are split into panels, each panel repeating the ID column.

wide <- paste0("options nocenter ls=64; data w; length ",
               paste(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), collapse = " "), " $8; ",
               paste0(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), "='xxxxxx';", collapse = " "),
               " run; proc print data=w noobs; run;")
cat(sas_run(wide)$listing, sep = "\n")
#> 
#>  v01       v02       v03       v04       v05       v06
#> 
#> xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx
#> 
#>  v07       v08       v09       v10       v11       v12
#> 
#> xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx    xxxxxx

What fails loud

sasonr stops with a sasonr_unsupported condition, naming the SAS line, for the layouts it does not implement yet, for example column panels with more than one observation, BY groups or SUM, and the page headers of a listing longer than one page under a small PAGESIZE=.

sas_run(paste0("options nocenter ls=64; data w; length ",
               paste(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), collapse = " "), " $8; ",
               paste0(sprintf("v%02d", 1:12), "='xxxxxx';", collapse = " "),
               " output; output; run; proc print data=w noobs; run;"))
#> Error in `sasonr_abort()`:
#> ! Unsupported: a PROC PRINT table wider than LINESIZE with more than one observation, BY groups, SUM or N (column panels measured on one observation)
